slides.header: Your notch, now an AI command center.
slides.subtitle: Dictation, meetings, screen help and 20 more tools. Private by default, pay once.
body: SparkV for macOS
Try Pro free for 14 days · sparkv.si
slides.notes: This is the MacBook notch. Most of us look straight past it. SparkV turns it into a drawer: hover, and your music, your files, your day and more than 20 AI agents slide out. The AI runs on your Mac, and Pro is a one-time purchase. Everything you will see today is the real app, not a mock-up.

slides.header: Your Mac work lives in six apps and six bills.
slides.subtitle: And the best spot on your screen does nothing.
body: Dictation, meeting notes, clipboard, screenshots, a launcher, a notch app.
Bought separately: about $492 in year one.
Monthly AI fees for work your Mac can do itself.
The notch: prime screen space, zero use.
body_min: Six apps. About $492 in year one.
Monthly AI fees for work your Mac can do itself.
The notch: prime screen space, zero use.
slides.notes: Think about the small tools a busy Mac user pays for: a dictation app, an AI meeting recorder, a clipboard manager, a screenshot tool, a launcher with AI, a notch app. Bought one by one, that comes to about four hundred and ninety-two dollars in the first year; slide 13 shows the breakdown. Many of those charge monthly for AI. Meanwhile, the notch sits in the middle of your screen doing nothing. [Figure = sum of year-one prices on slide 13; third-party listings, re-check before publishing.]

slides.header: Hover the notch. Everything is there.
slides.subtitle: One black drawer: media, files, your day, and a hub of 20+ agents.
body: Hover to open. Move away to close.
Drop any file on the notch.
Every agent is one click or one hotkey away.
slides.notes: Move the pointer onto the notch and the drawer opens; move away and it closes half a second later. The header switches pages: Home, Widgets, Tray, Today, Converter, Spaces. The grid icon opens the Agents hub, 22 tiles that launch every tool in SparkV. Most also have a hotkey, so you rarely need the mouse.

slides.notes: Here is what a normal day looks like. A meeting shows up under the notch ten minutes before it starts, with a Join button. One click records it; SparkV listens to your mic and the call audio, so no bot joins. At lunch you answer messages by voice. In the afternoon you convert a PDF without opening a website. You finish with focus rounds and a short recap. [Times are illustrative.]

slides.subtitle: All of this is in the free plan.
body: Media for any app: artwork glow, scrubber, bookmarks.
A Tray for files, with an AirDrop target.
Today: meetings with Join, plus a Pomodoro timer.
Live activities: volume, battery, notifications.
slides.notes: This is the free plan, and it is already a full notch app. Media controls work with any player that reports Now Playing. The Tray holds files you are moving between apps, with AirDrop built in. Today shows your next meetings with a Join button and runs a Pomodoro timer. When the drawer is closed, volume, battery and notifications appear as small live activities around the camera. [Live check required: media, tray drag, AirDrop, calendar, live activities.]

slides.subtitle: Hold fn anywhere. Talk. Release.
body: Dictation removes filler words and formats lists.
Reply Drafter (⌃⌥R) writes a reply in your tone. You press Send.
Prompt Refiner turns a rough ask into a clear AI prompt.
Add your own words so names are spelled right.
slides.notes: Put the cursor in any text field, hold fn, speak, let go. SparkV cleans up the text and types it in. Double-tap fn for hands-free. In Mail, Slack or Messages, Control-Option-R reads the thread and drafts a reply in your tone; you check it and press Send yourself. Prompt Refiner asks two to five quick questions and gives you a structured prompt for whichever AI tool you use. [Live check required: fn key, speech, Reply Drafter.]

slides.header: Ask about anything on your screen.
slides.subtitle: Works in any app, on any display.
body: Hold ⌃⌥ and ask. Clicky answers and points to the spot.
⌃⌥S: select a chart or an error, then ask about it.
⌃⌥T: copy text from images, videos and locked PDFs.
slides.notes: Stuck in an app you don't know? Hold Control-Option and ask out loud. Clicky looks at the screen under your mouse, answers out loud and in the band under the notch, and flies a pointer to the right spot. It points; it doesn't click for you. Control-Option-S lets you select part of the screen and ask about it. Control-Option-T copies the text out of anything: a screenshot, a video frame, a locked PDF. [Without an optional Groq key, Clicky reads screen text on device. Live check required.]

slides.header: Meeting notes, no bot in the call.
slides.subtitle: One click to record. Transcribed on your Mac.
body: Minutes, decisions and your tasks with due days.
A suggested answer when someone asks you a question.
Live translated captions, on device.
Filed into the right Space automatically.
slides.notes: Click the red button and SparkV records your microphone and the call's audio. Nothing joins the meeting. If someone asks you a question, a suggested answer appears under the notch. When you stop, you get minutes, decisions, your own tasks with due days, other people's tasks and the full transcript, filed into the right Space. Turn on Live Translation and other people's speech becomes captions in your language, translated on your Mac. [Live check required: audio capture, translation.]

slides.header: Every file, clip and note, one search away.
slides.subtitle: ⌥Space searches your Spaces, meetings, dictations, clipboard and Tray.
body: Clipboard history with a paste stack: ⌘⇧V.
Converter: PDF, image and document tools that work offline.
Downloads sorted by your rules as they finish.
Spaces: one memory per client or project, with cited answers.
slides.notes: Option-Space searches everything SparkV knows: Spaces, meetings, dictations, clipboard and Tray. Press Tab and it writes an answer from your own items with citations. Clipboard history is off until you turn it on, and it skips passwords; Command-Shift-V opens a paste stack right at your cursor. The Converter handles merge, split, compress, OCR and more without uploading anything. Downloads get sorted as they finish. [Search verified on sample data: 21 results for 'launch'. Downloads and drag need a live check.]

slides.subtitle: Focus rounds, one-click Modes and a nudge to sit back.
body: Focus: 25/5, 50/10 or 90/15 rounds, Do Not Disturb and a recap.
Modes: one click sets apps, wallpaper, volume and music. Turn it off to restore.
Screen Distance: a reminder when you sit closer than 40 cm.
slides.notes: Pick a rhythm and start Focus. SparkV turns on Do Not Disturb, runs the rounds, nudges you when you open a distracting app and writes a recap. A glowing border marks the start, breaks and the end. Modes switch your whole setup in one click, Study, Meeting, Presentation, and put everything back when you turn them off. Screen Distance is off by default; switch it on and it reminds you to move back from the screen. [Live check required: DND, glow, modes, camera.]

slides.header: Power tools for builders and job seekers.
slides.subtitle: Included in Pro.
body: UI Audit tests your own site and writes a fix prompt for your AI coding assistant.
Flow Canvas chains links, PDFs and notes into AI workflows.
Job Agent scores your fit and tracks every application.
Browser Flows (beta) records a web chore once and replays it.
slides.notes: Type your site's address into UI Audit and SparkV walks it like a tester: forms, buttons, mobile and desktop layouts, accessibility and console errors. One button copies a fix prompt you can paste into your AI coding assistant. Flow Canvas is a whiteboard for AI workflows. Job Agent saves a posting with fn plus Control and scores your fit against your resume. Browser Flows is in beta. UI Audit and Browser Flows need Node.js and only run on sites you own or may test. [UI Audit verified end to end; Job Agent scoring verified (fit 81% on sample data); Browser Flows self-test not clean.]
slides.requirements_note: Node.js required for UI Audit and Browser Flows

slides.notes: SparkV is built for Apple silicon Macs on macOS 15 or later, and it is best on a 14 or 16-inch MacBook Pro with a notch. On other displays the island sits in the menu bar. Apple last said there were over 100 million active Macs, back in 2018, and IDC estimates Apple shipped more than seven million Macs in the last quarter of 2025 alone. This is a large and growing group of people who already own the hardware. [Do not imply all of these Macs can run SparkV.]
